title: Zain Khan Moves Quietly While the Singhs Close In

blocks.text: Trying to avoid entrapment, Zain Khan advances carefully and suppresses the noise that would normally announce a commander on the move. Keeping all his war drums in the rear guard, he hopes to slip toward Sirhind before the Sikhs can concentrate fully against him.

That caution does not save him, because intelligence passes quickly among the Singh contingents. Majhail and Buddha Dal forces converge, musket fire opens, and the conversation among the Sikhs hardens into a common resolve that Zain Khan must be stopped outside the city.
The page is therefore about pursuit under pressure. One side relies on stealth and evasion; the other turns speed and memory of past wrongs into a tightening net.
